title: What is the difference between abstract classes and interfaces?
description: Understand when to use abstract classes vs interfaces.

data.text: **Question:** What is the difference between abstract classes and interfaces?

Abstract classes can have both abstract and concrete methods, support fields, and allow single inheritance. Interfaces define contracts with method signatures only (until recent C# versions added default implementations), and a class can implement multiple interfaces.

**Abstract Class:**
- Can have abstract and non-abstract methods
- Can have fields, constructors, destructors
- Supports access modifiers
- Single inheritance only
- Can provide base implementation

**Interface:**
- Only method signatures (historically)
- Can have default implementations (C# 8+)
- No fields (only properties)
- Multiple inheritance supported
- Pure contract definition
